figures.caption: Fig. 1. Distribution of residual membrane potential. The subplots demonstrate RMPD under distinct input distributions. Case (a) is dominated by the interval [ θ L , 2θ L ], while case (b) receives equal contributions from [0, θ L ] and [ θ L , 2θ L ]. Correspondingly, the RMP distribution in (a) exhibits near-Gaussian behavior, whereas the distribution in (b) severely departs from Gaussianity. Figure (c),(d) correspond to figure (a),(b) with smaller variance. Comparing case (c),(d) with (a),(b), we can tell that reducing variance of neuron input amplify the error-reduction effect.

Fig. 3. RMPD shapes before and after adjustment. Parameter QQ quantifies the similarity to Gaussian distribution, and it can be observed that the regularized RMPD is closer to Gaussian distribution after adjustment.
Fig. 4. Fine-tuning of initial membrane potential with shift compensation

Fig. 5. Architecture of SCR-Conv2d. The SCR-Conv2d layer is inserted after the standard convolutional layer. The outputs of the IF layer are transformed into refinement signal magnitudes via the nonlinear function Fnl. An additional IF layer is appended after SCR-Conv2d to maintain spike transmission. This figure illustrates the spike-driven information propagation pipeline of the converted SNN within VGG-16.
Fig. 6. Variations of Loss and LRMPD during fine-tuning on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet. LRMPD steadily decline, while Loss fluctuate mildly or rise slightly.
